title: Her Wedding
description:
When the hotel staff opened the heavy doors, chandelier light spilled out first.

A five-star hotel grand ballroom. Floral estimates, ye-dan lists, and guest-flow charts lay across the long table. Jiyeon stood in an ivory planning suit, holding one edge of the papers down with her fingertips. She looked composed as ever, except for the faint red at the tips of her ears.

His future father-in-law looked across the ballroom and said,
"It's my daughter's wedding. It has to be done without embarrassment. You understand that much, don't you?"

{name} understood that 'that much' exceeded his entire net worth. Jiyeon did not cut in right away. Instead she said, very low,
"Oppa, wait. Let's look at it ourselves first."

choices.text: "Yes. We'll look first, then decide." Meet her father's eyes.
choices.result_text:
Her father looked at {name} for a moment. It was the look of someone measuring him.

Jiyeon folded the file shut. "Oppa, this way." Her voice had gone thin and low. The ballroom carpet swallowed their footsteps as the two of them walked toward the seating-plan table.

choices.text: Look at Jiyeon's hand first. See whether she is shaking.
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon's fingers were gripping the edge of the file too hard. The paper had bent slightly.

She noticed {name}'s gaze and tried to smile, then failed. "It's okay. It's just... this is how my family does things." The end of the sentence came half a beat late.

She walked first to the seating-plan table. {name} followed.

description_if_known.told_jiyeon_about_records:
The Han family's wedding was on another scale.

A five-star hotel grand ballroom. The ye-dan alone ran to tens of millions of won. The guest list traded names from business and politics. His future father-in-law said,
"It's my daughter's wedding. It has to be done without embarrassment."

{name} knows where all of it — the ballroom, the ye-dan, those names — came from. Han PD Construction. The name at the bottom of a list, over a decade ago, that ruined his father.
And Jiyeon knows it now too.

They stand facing each other in a hall paid for with that money, both of them knowing. The groom's seats were still bare. {name} looked back and forth between those empty chairs and the bride's side across from them.
description_if_known.jiyeon_narrow_room:
The Han family's wedding was on another scale.

A five-star hotel grand ballroom. The ye-dan alone ran to tens of millions of won. The guest list traded names from business and politics. His future father-in-law said,
"It's my daughter's wedding. It has to be done without embarrassment. You understand that much, don't you?"

Standing in this wide ballroom, {name} suddenly thought of that narrow room. Two cup ramyeon, a fogged window. The night she said, "This room is like you, oppa — narrow, and all of it real."
Two people who knew that night now stood facing each other in a wide place with barely anything real in it.

The groom's seats were bare. {name} looked back and forth between those empty chairs and the bride's side across from them.
description_if_known.father_passed:
The Han family's wedding was on another scale.

A five-star hotel grand ballroom. The ye-dan alone ran to tens of millions of won. The guest list traded names from business and politics. His future father-in-law said,
"It's my daughter's wedding. It has to be done without embarrassment. You understand that much, don't you?"

{name} understood that 'that much' exceeded his entire net worth.

And the seating — the bride's side would fill with names everyone knew.
On the groom's list, {name} wrote down Hyunsu and left the rest blank. His hand stopped as he went to write his father's name. That seat, now, couldn't be filled — not even with a photo.

title: The Empty Side
description:
The seating chart was cruel in how neatly it was laid out.

The bride's side ran line after line with names everyone would recognize. Business, politics, real estate. Some would come to congratulate Jiyeon. Some would come to be seen at Chairman Han's daughter's wedding.

The groom's side had been left wide and blank. {name} held the pen and stopped for a long time. His father, Hyunsu, and empty space. The empty space looked clearer than people.

Jiyeon asked quietly,
"Oppa's side... is there no one else?"

choices.text: "If there isn't, then that's what we write." Do not hide the blanks.
choices.result_text:
The pen touched the paper. {name} did not borrow people who were not there.

Jiyeon looked at the groom's list, then the bride's list, then back at {name}. "That's like you, oppa." It sounded like praise, but the weight of the whole hall was folded inside it.

choices.text: "There are ways to fill it." Start calculating the blanks first.
choices.result_text:
{name} thought of hired guests, coworkers, even Jiyeon's company staff.

His head started counting seats before it counted people. Jiyeon seemed to notice. She said nothing. She only looked once at {name}'s hand on the papers, then looked away.

description_if_known.hyunsu_reconnected:
The seating chart was cruel in how neatly it was laid out.

The bride's side ran line after line with names everyone would recognize. The groom's side had been left wide and blank. {name} held the pen and stopped for a long time.

His father. Hyunsu. After those two names, his hand stopped. Still, those letters held out longer than a completely blank page.

Jiyeon asked quietly,
"Oppa's side... is there no one else?"

title: That Much
description:
Her father came back over. He pretended not to look at the list, but his face said he had already seen it.

"A wedding is between families," he said. "People will look at you. They'll look at the man standing beside my daughter."

Jiyeon drew breath half a beat too late. She looked as if she wanted to stop him, and as if she knew that world had lived inside her for too long.

{name} looked from the paper full of blanks to the estimate full of numbers. Now he had to choose. Stand in her world on tiptoe, or stand at his own height.

choices.text: "I'll make it work." Go into debt to stand at that level.
choices.result_text:
He took on debt to match the ye-dan, and filled the empty groom's seats with employees from Jiyeon's company.

A wedding without embarrassment. On the surface.

After the ceremony, {name} looked at his side again. Most were faces he didn't know.
He'd stood at the level of her world. On the very tips of his toes.

choices.text: "I can't do that. I want to do it within my means."
choices.result_text:
His father-in-law's face hardened. Jiyeon looked at {name} without a word.

"...It's fine. I've got you, oppa. That's all I need," Jiyeon said.
But at the end of those words, something flickered, just for a moment. Disappointment, or resignation.

{name} stood as himself. Only — the distance between her world and his became visible for the first time that day.

title: The Kind of Man He'd Be
description:
Five years are ending. Gangnam stayed out of reach.

For the first time in a while, Jiyeon sat him down, serious.
"I'll be honest, oppa. I never figured you for the kind of guy who'd live like this."

"I wasn't asking for anything huge. But you... somewhere along the way you just stopped. Dodging anything risky, settling for something small."

"I can't tell if that's stability or just giving up. My father calls it giving up."

Her eyes waited for an answer. Whatever {name} said now, this marriage hung on it.

choices.text: "I'll change. I'll fit your world. Anything." (Hold on to her)
choices.result_text:
From that day {name} decided to become someone else. He went into her father's business, learned the rules of that world, did things he never used to.

Jiyeon stayed. The marriage held.

But years later, looking in the mirror — the man standing there wasn't the one who ate triangle kimbap five years ago.
He kept her. Only, the man he kept her with was no longer himself.

choices.text: "This is me. I can't change it. ...I'm sorry." (Let her go)
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon looked at him for a long time. She didn't get angry. She wasn't the type.

"...I know. You're a good person, oppa. You're just not from my world."

She went back to her world. To a life that suited it, with someone who suited it.

{name} never reached Gangnam, and lost her too. But the face in the mirror was still his.
Small and whole, and traded for nothing.

choices.text: (Take out the phone — her first text, never deleted.)
choices.result_text:
Instead of answering, {name} took out his phone and set one old screen in front of her.
The first text, sent at dawn: "Am I kind of strange?"

Jiyeon looked down at the screen. One beat, two. The stern face slowly came undone.
"...You still have this?"
"I answered no back then. That answer hasn't changed." {name} said. "You're not a strange person — and I'm not a person who needs to change. We're both just built this way."

A long silence. Jiyeon looked out the window, then at the screen, then finally at {name}.
"...I'll talk to Dad myself." That was her answer.
Gangnam never came. But no one left, and no one changed. That night the two of them remained what they'd been at that dawn five years ago — two people who believed each other not strange.

description_if_known.namsan_lock_jiyeon:
Five years are ending. Gangnam stayed out of reach.

Jiyeon sat across from him, serious for once.
"I'll be honest. I didn't know you were someone who'd live like this."

Namsan came to mind. The night she called it childish and took a photo anyway, and hung the lock.
That lock would still be there. Whatever became of us.

Her eyes waited for an answer. On whatever {name} said now, this marriage hung.
